In the last block, `fee_delta <= parent_base_fee` I believe? Yeah the former is definitely fixed in your spec updates Btw going to merge your first PR, I hope you saw my latest comment! So I only have a minimum *increment* of 1. Was the assumption that we will also have a minimum *decrement* of 1? (I'm not sure at what point we move this conversation to <#692078615269212180>) Yeah I think the idea was a minimum magnitude to the increment, whether it is in the positive or negative direction Feel free to move it! I am going to be patchy with my responses here soon but will try to pick back up I'm probably wrong about that <@!680337202521440470> did the baseFee get down to 0 in the testnet by natural progression or purposely set to 0 to test that edge case? > <@!680337202521440470> did the baseFee get down to 0 in the testnet by natural progression or purposely set to 0 to test that edge case? <@!376568077950910466> no it naturally went down to 0. just running the testnet without transaction I wonder with the recent outstanding spec changes if that is still possible or not? I agree that the spec should be only frozen when everything works in the implementation 🙂 because in this case, the spec isn't actually that large We should start versioning the spec and match that up with PRs in Besu and go-ethereum so we know which is which. We should match the testnets to the spec versions. Does that make sense to everyone? We should cut releases for the testnets. Definitely, and I really don't like continuing calling different testnets the same name "YOLO" - that is just so confusing Yes, it's silly. some name which reflects the version of the code is better, as you suggest i would not mind it being silly, if it was helpful 🙂 Yeah, let's just version them EIP1559_n where n is the release and right now we should name what's running in testnet EIP1559_0 As an outsider, seeing the numerous EIP1559 changes on the EIP repository I was curious if there is any kind of versioning or indication of it. Happy with 1559_n 👍 Also, this can probably allow having testnets run with version `n` while we implement spec changes for version `n+1`, which is hard if everything is always running off master or ad-hoc commits.

Does the formula currently allow it to go negative?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
```python
if parent_gas_used == parent_gas_target:
    expected_base_fee = parent_base_fee
elif parent_gas_used > parent_gas_target:
    gas_delta = parent_gas_used - parent_gas_target
    fee_delta = max(parent_base_fee * gas_delta // parent_gas_target // BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR, 1)
    expected_base_fee = parent_base_fee + fee_delta
else:
    gas_delta = parent_gas_target - parent_gas_used
    fee_delta = parent_base_fee * gas_delta // parent_gas_used // BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR
    expected_base_fee = parent_base_fee - fee_delta
assert expected_base_fee == block.base_fee, 'invalid block: base fee not correct'
```
In the middle block, `fee_delta >= 0`.  In the last block, `fee_delta <= parent_base_fee` I believe?
